c2.evidence: NYS Clean Heat is the official NY state/utility heat-pump rebate program (ny.gov); federal 25C $2,000 credit confirmed EXPIRED 12/31/2025 by OBBBA (multiple 2026 sources).

c3.evidence: No fee to apply. Note: rebates require purchasing a heat-pump system ($5,000-$15,000+) through a participating contractor — it is a discount on spending, not income.

c4.evidence: Rebate typically applied at point of sale or paid through the participating contractor within weeks of installation; varies by utility territory.

s1.note: Varies by state/utility. NYS Clean Heat: 1-4 unit homes, NEEP-listed cold-climate equipment, participating contractor; income-eligible households (<=80% AMI) can stack EmPower+ support.

s2.note: Federal 25C credit ($2,000) is DEAD for 2026 installs — anyone promising it is wrong. State/utility amounts vary hugely; you must buy the system first; must use a participating contractor.

s3.note: Point-of-sale or post-installation payment via contractor; no single official date — varies by utility.

s4.note: The NYS incentive schedule is concrete per-Btu/h figures, not weasel-worded; program marketing elsewhere uses 'up to' language.

s5.note: https://cleanheatconnect.ny.gov/ — official NY state Clean Heat program site (ny.gov).

s6.note: Steps are concrete: check DSIRE/your utility for local heat-pump rebates, get quotes from participating contractors, install qualifying equipment, rebate via contractor.

payout_quote: ccASHP: Full Load Heating — $700 / $1,000 / $1,400 per 10,000 Btu/h of maximum heating capacity at 5F (categories 2 / 2a / 2b with decommissioning); Air-Source HPWH (<=120 gal): $1,000 per unit.
timing: Rebate applied at point of sale or paid through the participating contractor, typically within weeks of installation; varies by utility territory.
eligibility: State/utility-specific. NYS Clean Heat (exemplar, funded through 2030): homes with 1-4 units, qualifying cold-climate heat pump on the NEEP list, installed by a participating contractor. Other states/utilities (e.g., Xcel up to $2,000, CenterPoint $1,100) have their own rules. The expired federal 25C required meeting CEE highest-efficiency tier.
catches: The $2,000 federal heat-pump tax credit (25C) EXPIRED December 31, 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act — it is not available for 2026 installations.
Remaining rebates are state/utility-specific and vary from a few hundred to several thousand dollars; there is no national $2,000 offer anymore.
You must purchase a $5,000-$15,000+ system first — this is a discount on spending, not money earned.
Most programs require a participating contractor; DIY or non-listed equipment does not qualify.
steps: Look up heat-pump rebates for your zip code at https://dsireusa.org and on your electric/gas utility's website — amounts and rules are local.
Confirm the current program is funded and accepting applications (e.g., NYS Clean Heat runs through 2030; check your own state's status).
Get quotes only from contractors participating in your local rebate program and confirm the equipment model is on the program's qualifying list.
Install the qualifying heat-pump system; the rebate is applied at point of sale or paid through the contractor after installation.
Do NOT claim the federal 25C credit for any system placed in service after December 31, 2025 — it no longer exists.
biggest_catch: The $2,000 federal heat-pump tax credit expired December 31, 2025 — the remaining money is state/utility rebates that vary wildly and require buying a $5,000-$15,000 system through an approved contractor; it is a purchase discount, not income.
notes: CORRECTION vs the route's framing: the '$300-$2,000+' range is still real via state/utility rebates, but the $2,000 top end used to be the federal 25C credit, which is now dead.
